The Letterbox Forest Health and Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project will restore more open ponderosa pine forests by reducing excess vegetation, improving forest health and removing fuels that can carry flames into tree canopies. ELY, Nev. – The Bureau of Land Management began a wild horse gather Nov. 14, in and around the Antelope Complex Herd Management Area in northern Nevada, to protect the health of the herd as late season forage declines and winter approaches. The gather will help reduce the risks wild horses face when the range can no longer support the current population. The Antelope Complex includes the Antelope, Antelope Valley, Goshute, and Spruce-Pequop Herd Management Areas. Horses may appear healthy at the start of the fall, but forage and water resources are limited. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Boise District Office The Boise District, located in southwest Idaho, manages approximately 4 million acres of public land stretching from the central Idaho mountains to the borders with Oregon and Nevada. The District has many challenges to face as it balances its mission of multiple use and sustainable yield to achieve a sustainable ecosystem. Some of the major activities occurring within the district include: livestock grazing, wildland fire suppression, as well as motorized and non-motorized recreation. The Boise District is divided into three geographic areas/field offices: Bruneau (1.4 million acres), Four Rivers (1.3 million acres) and Owyhee (1.2 million acres). The District also manages Idaho's only National Conservation Area, Morley Nelson Snake River Birds of Prey (487,000 acres), home to the greatest concentration of nesting birds of prey in North America – and perhaps, the world. Some 800 pairs of hawks, owls, eagles and falcons come each spring to mate and raise their young here. What are the three branches of government? The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches: Legislative Judicial Executive This ensures that no individual or group will have too much power. Legislative branch The legislative branch is made up of Congress : The U.S. Senate The U.S. House of Representatives It also includes special agencies and offices that provide support services to Congress. The legislative branch’s key roles include: Drafting proposed laws Confirming or rejecting presidential nominations for heads of federal agencies, federal judges, and the Supreme Court Surveying the budget Having the authority to declare war Judicial branch The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts. It evaluates laws by: Interpreting the meaning of laws Applying laws to individual cases Deciding if laws violate the Constitution Executive branch The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch. The executive branch’s key roles include: The president is the head of state, leader of the executive branch, and commander in chief of the United States armed forces. The vice president supports the president. If the president is unable to serve, the vice president becomes president. Close BrandonSimons_Aloe's Diary Mapping the Southern African grid from OpenStreetMap, and where the gaps are Posted by BrandonSimons_Aloe on 17 November 2026 in English . I run Aloe Energy, a small not-for-profit initiative working on energy access in Sub-Saharan Africa. We published a free interactive map of the Southern African Power Pool grid, and OpenStreetMap is its backbone, so I wanted to share how it was built and where OSM could use help. What we did. We took every OSM power line of 66 kV and above across the 12 SAPP countries (country extracts from November 2026). Where OSM had no line but an older public map did, we filled the gap from TANESCO (2015) and World Bank (2017) grid maps, but only for lines recorded as existing, with a known voltage, and more than about 3 km from any OSM line. A “Source and age” view on the map colors each line by where it comes from, so you can see exactly what is OSM and what is gap-fill. Where OSM is thin. Coverage is weakest in Tanzania, DR Congo and Angola. Those are the places where the map still leans on maps that are close to ten years old, and where new mapping would change the picture most. Substations named in national plans are often missing too. The map: https://aloeenergy.org/research/sapp-grid . Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert October 23, 2026 5:00 AM ET Lars Gotrich Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castilllo/NPR A folk revival only goes so far as an artist's understanding — and adaptation — of tradition. What themes and melodies spoke to the past can easily echo into the present, but come alive through the personality of its interpreter. Brìghde Chaimbeul expands the language of the Scottish smallpipes behind the Desk with a quiet, yet demonstrative presence. Chaimbeul grew up on the Isle of Skye, Scotland, speaking Gaelic and learning the Highland pipes before falling in love with the bellows-blown bagpipe she plays today. Drones are forever with this instrument, but Chaimbeul amplifies, manipulates and darkens the harmonics and frequencies of these pipe drones with effects pedals and contact mics that capture her percussive tapping on the chanter. The effect is mystic and ancient … completely transfixing. Sponsor Message The rhythm of language permeates the songs chosen here — deeply knitting untranslatable wordplay into the drones and melodies. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/11/building-intelligence-first-responders-foundation-models-interoperable UPDATES Building Intelligence for First Responders: From Foundation Models to Interoperable Indoor Data November 5, 2026 Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email Credit: CTL When a disaster strikes outdoors, first responders are able to capture data from a variety of sources to adequately prepare their response. Satellite imagery, GIS, GPS, and drones all provide the ability to gather information about the scene. However, when a disaster happens indoors, none of those capabilities carry over. The available data becomes 2D, typically a blueprint if it exists, and does not include standpipes, shutoffs, alarm panels, or AEDs. These missing elements are necessary for a safe and timely response by first responders. Without indoor spatial intelligence, responders must make high stakes and high-risk decisions with incomplete information. Fixing the issue requires data that cannot be produced at scale and currently relies on manual documentation. However, many of these structures do not meet current building code requirements and require strategic upgrades. To address this vulnerability, NIST is actively developing best practices, design recommendations, and guidelines for utilizing building retrofit systems to improve the performance of existing structures. Beyond individual structures, it is critical to understand how different retrofit schemes and targets impact the community recovery. NIST is leading ongoing projects to quantify and measure the impact of various retrofit strategies at the community level. By developing the fundamental measurement science needed to assess retrofitted building performance, this work directly supports the long-term resilience and rapid recovery of communities following natural hazards. The docket also includes links to electronic images of most filings submitted to the court after November 13, 2017. To locate the docket for a particular case through a docket search, enter either the docket number for the case (e.g., 16-1523), or the names of one or more parties, or attorneys in the case. Overview A catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) occurs when germs enter the urinary tract through a urinary catheter and cause infection. CDC Statement on Increases in Recent Animal Rabies Activity and Associated Human Exposures Statement For immediate release: September 10, 2026 CDC Media Relations CDC Media Relations (404) 639-3286 media@cdc.gov https://www.cdc.gov/media/ Today, the CDC issued a Health Alert Network (HAN) health advisory to inform clinicians, health departments, and the public about increases in recent animal rabies activity and associated human exposures. Rabies is preventable when people who have been exposed receive appropriate administration of the rabies vaccine before symptoms begin. During the summer of 2026, reports of animal exposures and rabies post-exposure vaccinations have increased across the country. CDC urges clinicians to conduct careful, evidence-based rabies risk assessments and follow current ACIP recommendations when post-exposure vaccination or treatment is indicated. Proper administration of rabies vaccine and human rabies immune globulin is critical to ensuring patients receive effective protection while avoiding unnecessary treatment, costs, and strain on supplies.

pages.text: Census Bureau 101 for Students Census Bureau 101 for Students Skip Navigation Within About Us Census Bureau 101 for Students The U.S. Census Bureau is the leading source of information on the nation’s people, places, and economy, providing data about our country’s population size and growth as well as detailed portraits of the changing characteristics of our communities. The Census Bureau, part of the U.S. Department of Commerce, was created to address language in the Constitution on America’s need to count its population. America’s founders recognized that this information was needed to effectively serve its people. The data collected as part of the first count in 1790 — a six-question survey — expanded in the following years to include information on the economy, immigration, migration, and agriculture. One of the most important ways all of this information has been used is to determine apportionment of the seats in the U.S. House of Representatives. The count of the U.S. population — carried out every 10 years — is called the Decennial Census of Population and Housing. During the decennial census, the Census Bureau contacts every household, asking questions such as: How many people live or stay in this house, apartment, or mobile home? What is the name of the person who owns this house, apartment, or mobile home? How old is the person who owns this house, apartment, or mobile home? When is his or her birthday? Professional employer organizations (PEOs) handle various payroll administration and tax reporting responsibilities for their business clients and are typically paid a fee based on payroll costs. Pursuant to section 7705(a) of the Internal Revenue Code, the term “certified professional employer organization” (CPEO) means a person that applies to be certified as a CPEO and that the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) has certified as meeting the applicable requirements. The Tax Increase Prevention Act of 2014, enacted December 19, 2014, requires the IRS to establish a voluntary certification program for PEOs which is the CPEO Program.
